Hi Tom,

Hope you're doing well — our records show Atlas AI's Dedicated Reserved capacity is up for renewal the week of Nov 23. You mentioned interest in doubling to 32 GPUs to support the new inference batch we discussed.

Attached is a short renewal summary (renewal_summary_v3.pdf) showing current utilization, the proposed 16→32 upgrade, and a baseline estimate for reserved per-hour pricing. Quick highlights:
- 12-month committed term (preferred) or 24-month term available
- Proposed reserved per-GPU hourly rate: $2.85/hr (preliminary)
- Burst capacity available with autoscale; we can bake in throughput SLOs per the attached sample SLA

If Atlas wants to proceed, I can schedule a 30-min call this week to walk through the numbers and get procurement next steps.

Thanks,
Grace

Grace — thanks for the summary. A few immediate questions from procurement / ops: 

1) Can you confirm the per-hour reserved price if we go to 32 GPUs and commit for 12 months? The $2.85/hr looks like the current estimate but we need final numbers for our TCO model.
2) Throughput guarantees — we need a clear SLO (tokens/sec or inference/sec) and a remediation/credit policy if you miss it.
3) We will need a separate line-item quote for 32 GPUs + any committed-hour discount and an exportable quote for our finance team (PDF + spreadsheet).

Also, curious whether Redwood will include any onboarding credits or short-term usage credits if we sign early. Can we set up a call with Marcus or Sales Engineering to walk the technical side?

—Tom
Tom Reed
VP Product Operations, Atlas AI
procurement@atlasai.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-11T11:32:00-08:00
Subject: FW: Atlas AI renewal — pricing suggestion for 32 GPUs

Grace / team — looping you in with a draft commercial approach for Atlas. Notes below; attached is a working quote (quote_AtlasAI_32gpu_draft.xlsx).

Commercial proposal (draft):
- SKU: Dedicated Reserved Pool — 32x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Term: 12 months (option to extend to 24 months at additional 3% discount)
- Revised reserved per-GPU hourly rate (32 GPU block): $2.40/hr (volume discount applied)
- Committed monthly minimum: 24,000 GPU-hours
- Burst capacity: +20% at pay-as-you-go rate ($3.20/hr) with automatic fallback policies
- Onboarding credit: $8,000 applied against first invoice if signed by Nov 30

SLA / throughput: propose a guaranteed median throughput of 110 inferences/sec per GPU for typical 2k-token workloads, measured as 5-min windowed median. Credit policy: 5% service credit for monthly rolling windows where observed median falls below 95% of target for more than 6 hours.

As far as strategy, I recommend we lock the 12-month price at $2.40/hr for the 32-GPU block — it's aggressive but keeps the unit economics attractive and buys the deal. Marissa / Finance: do we need to route this through a formal approval or legal redline given the onboarding credit?

Attachments: quote_AtlasAI_32gpu_draft.xlsx

--Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: Atlas AI renewal — pricing suggestion for 32 GPUs

Quick technical clarifications to support the SLA wording: 

- Measurement: We'll publish a per-route telemetry view (Console) and provide CSV exports for monthly measurement. Throughput target = 110 inferences/sec per GPU for 2k-token avg payload — can be expressed as 6600 inferences/sec for the 32-GPU pool.
- Safety margin: recommend we set operational guardrails (auto-burst thresholds, continuous batching off-peak) to hit sustained throughput while preserving latency SLOs.
- Fallback: If the reserved pool is constrained, automatic routing to a compatible smaller-quantized model with a 10% degraded throughput must be clearly called out. Should be in the ops addendum.

We can include the draft SLA text in the quote PDF. No blockers from our side — only ask that the SLO measurement windows and instrumentation be spelled out.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
